verdict_reason: The edits follow the frontend's new Latin-name chips and scoped no-results text correctly, but the commodity-heading assertion was loosened to a regex that cannot fail if the named heading regresses, and the helper it calls is misnamed.

todos.issue: The heading assertion was loosened, not updated. commodities.spec.ts:63 now checks each group against commodityHeading(code), the regex ^(.+ \()?<code>\)?$ (commodity-selection-page.ts:61-63). It passes for the old bare-code legend ('0102'), for any name at all ('Anything (0102)'), and for unbalanced text ('0102)', 'Cow (0102'). The frontend now heads groups 'Cow (0102)' via namedLegendFor (commodity-legend.js:5-8), so reverting that change leaves this test green, and the title's claim 'lists ... groups by commodity heading' is proven only for the code part.
todos.fix: Must: the test fails if a commodity group's heading is not exactly the heading the page is meant to show, the name and code in brackets for a named commodity and the code alone for an unnamed one. One way: add a test-data map of expected headings for the codes GROUPING_QUERIES returns (for example 0102 -> 'Cow (0102)', 01061900 -> '01061900') and assert toHaveAccessibleName(expectedHeading, exact); keep the regex only for locating groups, or have commodityGroup take the exact heading.

todos.issue: commodityHeading(code), called at commodities.spec.ts:63 and defined at commodity-selection-page.ts:61-63, does not return a heading. It returns a RegExp that matches any heading ending in the code. Its parameter 'code' also takes a regex fragment: commodityGroups passes '\\d+' (commodity-selection-page.ts:70), and a real code is put into the pattern without escaping. A reader of line 63 would expect an exact heading string.
todos.fix: Must: the page-object member the spec calls says it returns a pattern for matching headings, and its parameter says whether it takes a commodity code or a regex fragment. One way: rename it commodityHeadingPattern and split it so commodityGroups builds its own any-code pattern, or remove it if the first finding's exact expected headings replace it.
